beats.text: It's eighteen thirty-three. A ship leaves Boston for India, loaded with one hundred eighty tons of ice.
The trip takes four months, straight across the equator.
The ice was cut from frozen lakes and packed in sawdust.
But when the ship reached Calcutta, a hundred tons were still frozen.
So people in India drank ice-cold drinks, from American lakes.
Then came ice houses, ice ships, and finally the fridge.
Today, your freezer makes ice in a few hours, right in your kitchen.
One hundred eighty tons crossed the world, so someone could have a cold drink.

sources: Ship Tuscany left Boston on 12 May 1833 with about 180 tons of ice packed in sawdust; arrived in Calcutta in early September 1833 with about 100 tons still frozen, after about four months. Frederic Tudor ('the Ice King'). American Heritage, 'Cold Mine'; Atlas Obscura, 'How did people get ice'; Scroll.in.
